ordered_diagnoses: Squamous cell carcinoma of the ureter

s1.syndrome_frame: intermittent pelvic pain and gross hematuria with ureteral obstruction
salient_findings: tubular filling defect with partial obstruction of the right mid ureter
key_facts: renal ultrasound and cystoscopy showed no abnormalities
tubular filling defect with partial obstruction of the right mid ureter
5 cm long tubular mass in the mid ureter
urine cytology and endoscopic biopsy were negative for malignancy
slight dilatation of the right renal pelvis
subtle thickening of the right ureter
no evidence of metastasis or lymphadenopathy

shortlist: Squamous cell carcinoma of the ureter

shortlist.label: Ureteral transitional cell carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: most common ureteral tumor, consistent with hematuria and ureteral obstruction

shortlist.label: Ureteral fibroepithelial polyp
shortlist.why_kept: benign tumor, can cause ureteral obstruction and hematuria, consistent with negative biopsy

shortlist.label: Ureteral leiomyoma
shortlist.why_kept: benign tumor, can cause ureteral obstruction and hematuria, less common than fibroepithelial polyp

shortlist.label: Ureteral inflammatory myofibroblastic tumor
shortlist.why_kept: rare tumor, can cause ureteral obstruction and hematuria, negative biopsy does not rule out

shortlist.label: Squamous cell carcinoma of the ureter
shortlist.why_kept: less common than transitional cell carcinoma, but still a consideration with hematuria and ureteral obstruction

raw.rationale: The presence of a pedunculated ureteral tumor with a vulnerable surface and negative urine cytology and endoscopic biopsy for malignancy suggests a benign lesion, making Ureteral fibroepithelial polyp a likely diagnosis.

rejected.label: Ureteral transitional cell carcinoma
rejected.why: Negative urine cytology and endoscopic biopsy for malignancy

rejected.label: Ureteral leiomyoma
rejected.why: Less common and not typically pedunculated

rejected.label: Ureteral inflammatory myofibroblastic tumor
rejected.why: Not typically described as pedunculated and often associated with inflammation

rejected.label: Squamous cell carcinoma of the ureter
rejected.why: Negative urine cytology and endoscopic biopsy for malignancy, and squamous cell carcinoma is less common in the ureter
